brief.question: Do the complete reduced cubic and quartic Hamiltonian functionals agree with exact Gaussian/Gaunt identities, rotational invariants and independently evaluated finite-metric curvature?
brief.from_parent: The parent validated the ten-mode TT basis, the reduced canonical map and a single momentum-direction energy expansion. This child derives full H3/H4, including scalar conformal and longitudinal York responses, on that same declared reduction-first candidate.
brief.healthy: Seven exact directions pass TT, integrated-curvature, Gram, York inverse and Fourier normalization checks. Two cubic and five quartic potential invariants reproduce held-out directions. A rational SO(3) rotation leaves all energy terms unchanged. Four independent finite-metric cases extrapolate the curvature and projection ingredients with scaled error below 1e-10.
brief.noise: The actual finite-metric error is the raw signal; its view label displays units of 1e-12. Cubic and quartic coefficients are in different declared Gaussian units. The physical rank stays N=3 with one radial profile per parity. Exact zero is expected for identity residuals. No claim of an amplitude, controlled interacting limit or full interacting reconstruction follows.
brief.worth_a_flag: A rational identity or held-out invariant check fails, the independent finite-metric error exceeds 1e-10, the metric determinant or connection trace exceeds 1e-50, or progress stops during exact algebra. Negative quartic coefficients are not by themselves a failure: the weak-field polynomial is not a globally bounded Hamiltonian.
brief.decided: Local CPU, Python standard library, inherited fixed recipe. Seven exact directions and four 70-digit finite-metric checks, using 32 finite amplitudes. No separate trial changes the source before launch. Preserve a meaningful source snapshot permanently; review actual logs on the next turn.
